title: Book Three · Chapter 173: The Two Packets Go
story:
On Monday morning, Ronan meets Anna outside the post office.

The summer holiday is nearly over. Each has a flat packet under one arm.

Ronan's holds his completed form, his short letter, and the teacher's note. Anna's holds her form and the four drawing copies. Her originals are safe at home.

They check the addresses before they go inside.

The coastal packet must arrive by the last Friday in October. Anna's deadline is the second Friday in November. They are sending both well before those dates.

“Three pieces?” Anna asks.

Ronan nods. “Form, letter, teacher's note.”

“And my five sheets.”

She touches the form above her four drawings. Each drawing has her name and a short description at the bottom.

The first application requires no fee at either place. Class payments come later, after a decision and an accepted place.

At the window, each pays the postage for their own packet. Ronan uses his separate spending money. Anna uses her own saved money.

His work and study envelopes stay at home.

The clerk takes the packets. Ronan watches the coastal address go into the post bag. Then Anna's design-school address follows it.

They have submitted the applications now. They have no reply about arrival yet, and no decision.

Outside, Anna takes a slow breath.

“I keep thinking about the stair.”

“The sizes are there.”

“I know. I still keep thinking.”

Ronan looks at the empty space beneath her arm. He remembers the large drawing packet under her arm on their way here.

“You can put your arm down now.”

Anna laughs and lets it fall beside her.

“It still feels like the paper is there.”

He knows the feeling. Before they left the window, he almost asked the clerk to let him count the three pieces once more.

“The form is in yours?” he asks.

“Yes. We checked it.”

She says it gently. He smiles at himself and looks back at the post office door.

Their packets are inside now. They cannot make another corner darker or change one word at this moment.

Anna moves her empty hand beside his.

“The fruit shop can travel without me.”

“The stair too.”

She laughs again. The words help a little. They leave the door behind them. The first notes of a guitar come from the road. Ronan turns toward the sound.

Ronan gives her his hand. They walk toward the small square near the market.

A man is playing a guitar beneath a tree. A few people have stopped to listen. Ronan and Anna sit on the low wall at the edge.

For a while, she watches the player's hands. Ronan listens to the words. The song is new to him, and he misses part of the first line.

When it comes again, he can follow it.

Anna moves closer. Her drawing bag is empty now, except for her notebook and pencil case.

“No more fruit in the envelope,” Ronan says.

She laughs and rests her shoulder against his.

They stay until the song finishes. Then Anna needs to meet Lin, and Ronan has his own last holiday task at home.

At the corner, she squeezes his hand before she lets go. He lifts a hand as she turns toward Lin's street.

Ronan walks home with his own packet copies in his bag. The roof bookmark is between their pages, and he keeps the bag close as he passes the crowded market entrance.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

submit＝正式提交；postage＝邮资；description＝说明、描述；decision＝决定、申请结果。

## 理解问题

1. 两人的申请包分别包含什么、寄往哪里？邮资各从哪里付？
2. 这时已经完成提交，还是已确认收到或录取？他们在等待哪个阶段？

## 读句子

**They have submitted the applications now.**

拆开看：They / have submitted / the applications / now.

他们／已经正式提交／各自的申请／到本章投邮时完成这一步。
